intro: 1.9 is a release for keeping what you read. A journal kept by the Church's day, free for everyone; every verse opened to its Greek, and with Purify Plus to its cross-references and the other Bibles; five more Bibles to download; and plans to read the Scriptures through the year.

sections.heading: Your journal, by the Church's day
sections.body: Today's page shows the day's feast or saints and its readings, each with a pen to begin a page about it. Write freely, add verse cards and your highlights, and quote anything in Purify into it with Quote in journal. The journal is free for everyone. It is in Export your library, and on the website you can print it or save it as a PDF. Share a page as a copy at a link of its own, three a month, and Stop sharing takes it down at once. Purify Plus adds covers from the icons, notebooks and tags, blocks and styles, sharing without limit, and on a computer your notebooks at the side.

sections.heading: Every verse, opened
sections.body: Tap a verse to open it: highlight it, copy it, share it as a picture, write a note, and see its Greek. A Remember the verse widget keeps your verse on your home screen. With Purify Plus, study the verse with its cross-references, which now reach into the Old Testament in the Septuagint, tap a word to study its Greek, remember the verse in three steps, the missing words, then the first letters, then from memory, spaced over the days that follow, and with Compare see it in every Bible you can download and in the Greek, each at the place its own numbering puts it.

sections.heading: Five more Bibles
sections.body: From the translations list you can download the Russian Synodal (1876), the Greek Septuagint with the Patriarchal text (1904), the Serbian of Karadžić and Daničić (1868), the Arabic Van Dyck (1865) and the Spanish Reina-Valera (1909), each read in its own numbering. The Arabic and the Spanish are Protestant translations, and are labelled so. Psalms 113 to 115 are now divided as the Septuagint divides them, like the rest of the Psalter, and your notes, highlights, saved and gathered verses, and the verse cards in your journal move with their verses.

sections.heading: Plans, and the Florilegium
sections.body: In Purify Plus, new plans: John in 21 days, Acts in 28 days, the New Testament in a year, the Nativity Fast with the Church's own readings for the fast, and Holy Week, nearly every day with a passage of the Fathers on it. The plans page keeps your place, puts the season's plan at the top and shows every plan with its picture. The Florilegium shows your gatherings as cards, brings a line from them to Today, and hands a gathering on as a booklet. If your Purify Plus ends, the gatherings in your Florilegium stay yours to read.

sections.heading: History, the Creed and Today
sections.body: The Creed by council sets the Symbol of Faith out article by article, with the words the Council of Constantinople added lit. On the days an event of Orthodox History fell, it is on Today under the saint of the day. Orthodox History shows its great events as large cards, every picture for every reader, and its map puts each event where its own account says. With Purify Plus, the Thread walks 35 events step by step on their maps, year by year.

sections.heading: Listening, Candlelight and the rest
sections.body: Listening keeps one card at rest and a small pill as you scroll, and keeps your place in every book. In Purify Plus, saved books are marked, a chant can be kept on your phone as a book is, each book's size shows before you save it, saving waits for Wi-Fi and picks up after a lost signal, and on Android the week's readings are kept offline by themselves; Candlelight lights the lines you are reading and can come on at Vespers; ambience plays two sounds at once; and two palettes are earned by reading, Councils and Cappadocian. Every field's hint is easier to read, the day's prayer hours no longer fade, the shop's photos load as you browse, the words under the player's buttons fit in every language, and a handful of small things were put right.
